items.text: Noah built an ark to survive the flood.
items.note: God commands Noah to build the ark.

items.text: Jonah was swallowed by a whale.
items.note: The Bible speaks of a "great fish," not a whale.

items.text: David defeated Goliath with a sword.
items.note: He defeated him with a sling and a stone.

items.text: Jesus was born in Bethlehem.
items.note: As the prophet Micah had announced.

items.text: The Ten Commandments were given by God to Moses.
items.note: On Mount Sinai.

items.text: The Bible says there were exactly three wise men.
items.note: The text does not specify their number, only three gifts.

items.text: Adam and Eve ate an apple.
items.note: The Bible says "the fruit," without specifying which one.

items.text: Jesus turned water into wine at Cana.
items.note: His very first miracle.

items.text: Jesus chose twelve apostles.
items.note: Twelve, like the tribes of Israel.

items.text: The first book of the New Testament is Genesis.
items.note: It's the Gospel of Matthew; Genesis opens the Old Testament.

items.text: Samson's strength came from his hair.
items.note: He loses it when Delilah has it cut off.

items.text: The word "Trinity" appears as such in the Bible.
items.note: The reality is taught, but the word doesn't appear in it.

items.text: Jesus walked on water.
items.note: And Peter too, for a moment.

items.text: Judas betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.
items.note: The price of a slave.

items.text: The Bible says money is the root of all evil.
items.note: It's the "love of money" that's at issue, not money itself.

items.text: Abraham was willing to offer his son Isaac.
items.note: God stops him and provides a ram.

items.text: The people of Israel wandered forty years in the desert.
items.note: An entire generation.

items.text: Jesus rose on the third day.
items.note: The heart of the Gospel.

items.text: Goliath was an Israeli soldier.
items.note: He was a Philistine giant, enemy of Israel.

items.text: Peter denied Jesus three times.
items.note: Before the rooster crowed.

items.text: Noah's ark came to rest on Mount Sinai.
items.note: It came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.

items.text: Jesus fed five thousand men with five loaves and two fish.
items.note: Twelve baskets remained.

items.text: The book of Psalms contains one hundred psalms.
items.note: It contains one hundred fifty.

items.text: Eve was formed from one of Adam's ribs.
items.note: To be a helper suitable for him.

items.text: Moses entered the Promised Land.
items.note: He saw it from afar; it was Joshua who brought the people into it.

items.text: The walls of Jericho fell after seven laps.
items.note: On the seventh day, after seven laps and a great shout.

items.text: Daniel was cast into a fiery furnace.
items.note: Daniel was cast into the lion's den; the furnace was for his three friends.

items.text: The Holy Spirit came down on the disciples at Pentecost.
items.note: With tongues of fire.

items.text: The Bible was written by a single author.
items.note: About forty authors over approximately 1,500 years.

items.text: Elijah was taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire.
items.note: Elisha receives his mantle.

items.text: Jesus' first miracle was the resurrection of Lazarus.
items.note: His first miracle was turning water into wine at Cana.

items.text: Solomon asked God for wisdom.
items.note: Rather than wealth or a long life.

items.text: It rained forty days and forty nights during the flood.
items.note: The waters covered everything.

items.text: Cain killed his brother Abel.
items.note: The first murder, out of jealousy.

items.text: The ten plagues struck the people of Israel.
items.note: They struck Egypt, to free Israel.

items.text: Jesus was baptized by John the Baptist in the Jordan.
items.note: The Spirit descends like a dove.

items.text: The fruit of the Spirit includes love, joy, and peace.
items.note: Also patience, kindness…

items.text: Zacchaeus was a man of very great height.
items.note: He was short; he climbed a tree to see Jesus.

items.text: The Bible ends with the book of Revelation.
items.note: The vision of the renewed world.

items.text: Thomas doubted the resurrection of Jesus.
items.note: "If I don't see… I won't believe."

items.text: The Protestant Bible contains sixty-six books.
items.note: Thirty-nine in the Old, twenty-seven in the New.

items.text: Jesus died by stoning.
items.note: He was crucified under Pontius Pilate.

items.text: Mary was the mother of Jesus.
items.note: The angel Gabriel announces it to her.

items.text: Jesus raised his friend Lazarus.
items.note: After four days in the tomb.

items.text: King David was a shepherd in his youth.
items.note: The youngest of the sons of Jesse.

items.text: Paul wrote a letter to the Romans.
items.note: One of his greatest epistles.

items.text: Esau sold his birthright for a plate of lentils.
items.note: To his brother Jacob.

items.text: Jesus said: "I am the way, the truth, and the life."
items.note: "No one comes to the Father except through me."

items.text: There are four gospels in the New Testament.
items.note: Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John.

items.text: Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed by an earthquake.
items.note: By a rain of sulfur and fire.

items.text: There were three wise men at the birth of Jesus.
items.note: The Bible speaks of wise men from the East, without specifying their number.

items.text: Judas betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of gold.
items.note: They were pieces of silver.

items.text: Jesus' first miracle was multiplying the loaves.
items.note: His first miracle was turning water into wine at Cana.

items.text: Paul was called Saul before his conversion.
The apostle Paul was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus.
items.note: Paul was called after the resurrection; he was not one of the twelve.

items.text: Mount Sinai is also called Mount Horeb.
Elijah died and was buried.
items.note: He was taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire.

items.text: The son Abraham offered in sacrifice was Ishmael.
items.note: It was Isaac.

items.text: Eight people were saved in Noah's ark.
There were twelve plagues in Egypt.
items.note: There were ten.

items.text: The golden calf was made by Aaron.
David was the youngest of the sons of Jesse.
Solomon asked God for wealth.
items.note: He asked for wisdom.

items.text: The Queen of Sheba came to visit David.
items.note: She came to see Solomon.

items.text: The three friends of Daniel were named Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
Jonah was sent to preach in Babylon.
items.note: He was sent to Nineveh.

items.text: John the Baptist fed on locusts and wild honey.
Jesus was baptized by the apostle Peter.
items.note: He was baptized by John the Baptist.

items.text: Jesus fasted forty days in the desert.
Lazarus remained dead four days before being raised.
Zacchaeus was a Pharisee.
items.note: He was a chief tax collector.

items.text: Simon of Cyrene carried the cross of Jesus.
Thomas put his finger in the wounds of the risen Jesus.
On the day of Pentecost, the Spirit came down in the form of tongues of fire.
Stephen was the first Christian martyr.
Revelation was written by the apostle Paul.
items.note: It was written by John.

items.text: The evangelist Luke was a physician.
The apostle Matthew was a fisherman.
items.note: He was a tax collector.

items.text: Peter cut off the ear of a servant during the arrest of Jesus.
The servant whose ear Peter cut off was named Malchus.
Barabbas was released instead of Jesus.
Nicodemus came to see Jesus at night.
The Good Samaritan in the parable was a priest.
items.note: He was a Samaritan.

items.text: After the multiplication of the loaves, twelve baskets of pieces remained.
Goliath was an Amalekite.
items.note: He was a Philistine.

items.text: King Saul consulted a sorceress at En-Dor.
Absalom died with his hair caught in a terebinth.
Solomon's temple was built in seven years.
Elijah faced 450 prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel.
Naaman the leper dipped himself seven times in the Nile.
items.note: He dipped himself in the Jordan.

items.text: King Nebuchadnezzar lived like an animal for a time.
The handwriting on the wall appeared at the feast of King Belshazzar.
The first king of Israel was David.
items.note: The first king was Saul.

items.text: The prophet Samuel anointed David as king.
Methuselah is the oldest man mentioned in the Bible.
items.note: 969 years old.

items.text: Enoch was taken up by God without knowing death.
Sarah gave birth to Isaac in her old age.
The flood lasted forty days and forty nights of rain.
The burning bush burned without being consumed.
The prodigal son squandered his inheritance and then returned to his father.
The Last Supper was a Passover meal.
Pontius Pilate handed Jesus over to be crucified.
Bathsheba was the wife of Uriah the Hittite.
The prophet Hosea married an unfaithful woman, Gomer.
Jericho was the first city conquered in Canaan.
The prophet Elisha was the servant of Elijah.
Mary Magdalene was the mother of Jesus.
items.note: The mother of Jesus was Mary.

items.text: The book of Psalms is the longest book in the Bible.
items.note: 150 chapters.

items.text: The Protestant Bible contains 66 books.
The Mount of Olives is where Jesus was crucified.
items.note: He was crucified at Golgotha.

items.text: Job lost all his possessions and his children but kept his faith.
Ezekiel saw a valley of dry bones that came to life.
Jacob had twelve sons who gave rise to the tribes of Israel.
King Herod had John the Baptist beheaded.
Solomon wrote the book of Song of Songs.
Lot's wife looked back and was turned into a pillar of salt.
Melchizedek was both a king and a priest.
There are 27 books in the New Testament.
Paul wrote the epistle to the Romans.
The giant Og, king of Bashan, slept in an iron bed.
Gideon defeated the Midianites with only three hundred men.
The first murder in the Bible was committed by Cain against Abel.
The prophet Daniel interpreted the dreams of King Nebuchadnezzar.
Jesus himself wrote several books of the New Testament.
items.note: Jesus left no writings; the gospels were written by others.

items.text: Moses entered the Promised Land with the people.
items.note: He died before, seeing the land from Mount Nebo.

items.text: The giant Goliath was killed by King Saul.
items.note: It was David who killed Goliath.

items.text: Moses wrote the book of Revelation.
items.note: Revelation was written by John.

items.text: God created the world in seven days before resting.
items.note: Creation took six days; rest came on the seventh.

items.text: Jesus was born in Nazareth.
items.note: Jesus was born in Bethlehem.

items.text: The Ten Commandments were given on Mount Carmel.
items.note: They were given on Mount Sinai.

items.text: King David built the temple of Jerusalem.
items.note: It was his son Solomon who built it.

items.text: Abraham was the father of Moses.
items.note: They are separated by several centuries.

items.text: Saul became king after David.
items.note: Saul reigned before David.

items.text: Cain was the son of Noah.
items.note: Cain was the son of Adam and Eve.

items.text: The Hebrews wandered ten years in the desert.
items.note: They wandered there for forty years.

items.text: The apostle Paul was a fisherman by trade.
items.note: Paul was a tentmaker.

items.text: Jesus was crucified with only one thief.
items.note: He was crucified between two thieves.

items.text: Ruth was an Egyptian.
items.note: Ruth was a Moabite.

items.text: Jesus fed five thousand women with five loaves.
items.note: He fed five thousand men, not counting women and children.

items.text: Jesus' baptism took place in the Sea of Galilee.
items.note: He was baptized in the Jordan.

items.text: King Nebuchadnezzar was king of Egypt.
items.note: He was king of Babylon.

items.text: The book of Acts was written by the apostle Peter.
items.note: It was written by Luke.

items.text: The prophet Daniel was cast into a fiery furnace.
items.note: Daniel was cast into the lion's den.

items.text: Joshua made the walls of Babylon fall.
items.note: He made the walls of Jericho fall.

items.text: At Cana, Jesus turned wine into water.
items.note: He turned water into wine.

items.text: There are fifty psalms in the Bible.
items.note: The book of Psalms contains 150.

items.text: The angel who announced the birth of Jesus to Mary was named Michael.
items.note: It was the angel Gabriel.

items.text: Lazarus, raised by Jesus, was the brother of Peter.
items.note: He was the brother of Martha and Mary.

items.text: Judas Iscariot was replaced by Barnabas.
items.note: He was replaced by Matthias.

items.text: The son Abraham was about to sacrifice was Jacob.
items.note: It was Isaac.

items.text: The prophet Isaiah was swallowed by a great fish.
items.note: It was Jonah who was swallowed.

items.text: Pharaoh freed the Hebrews after the first plague.
items.note: He let them go after the tenth plague.

items.text: The twelve spies all returned confident from exploring Canaan.
items.note: Ten were discouraged; only Joshua and Caleb had faith.

items.text: Mount Ararat is where Moses received the Law.
items.note: The ark came to rest there; the Law was given on Sinai.

items.text: Jesus remained forty years in the desert before his ministry.
items.note: He remained there forty days.

items.text: Manna fell on the day of the Sabbath.
items.note: It did not fall on the Sabbath; a double portion fell the day before.

items.text: The first person mentioned as dead in the Bible is Adam.
items.note: Abel, killed by Cain, dies first in the account.

items.text: Solomon succeeded his son Rehoboam.
items.note: It was Rehoboam who succeeded Solomon.

items.text: The prophet Elijah faced the prophets of Baal on Mount Sinai.
items.note: It was on Mount Carmel.

items.text: Mary, mother of Jesus, was the wife of Joseph of Arimathea.
items.note: She was the wife of Joseph the carpenter.

items.text: King Herod worshipped the child Jesus in Bethlehem.
items.note: Herod sought to have him killed.

items.text: Peter walked on water without ever sinking.
items.note: He began to sink and cried out for help.

items.text: There are ten apostles in the New Testament.
items.note: Jesus chose twelve apostles.

items.text: Goliath was about one meter fifty tall.
items.note: He was about three meters tall.

items.text: The golden calf was made by Joshua while Moses was away.
items.note: It was made by Aaron.

items.text: The Tower of Babel was built after crossing the Red Sea.
items.note: It was built much earlier, at the origins of nations.

items.text: The prophet Nathan rebuked David after his sin with Bathsheba.
Daniel refused the king's food and yet remained in good health.
Jesus raised the daughter of Jairus from the dead.
Peter was delivered from prison by an angel.
The prophet Amos was a shepherd before he was called.
The city of Nineveh repented at the preaching of Jonah.
Jesus healed a man blind from birth by applying mud to his eyes.
King Josiah was eight years old when he became king.
Abraham received three visitors near the oaks of Mamre.
Elisha healed Naaman of leprosy.
Jesus multiplied seven loaves for four thousand men.
Mary and Joseph found Jesus in the temple when he was twelve years old.
God set a mark on Cain so that no one would kill him.
Jacob worked fourteen years in total for Leah and Rachel.
The apostle Paul was shipwrecked near the island of Malta.
Jesus washed his disciples' feet before his death.
King Solomon received a visit from the Queen of Sheba.
Elijah was fed by ravens at the Kerith Brook.
Jesus calmed a storm on the Sea of Galilee.
The veil of the temple was torn in two at Jesus' death.
King Solomon had only one son named David.
items.note: David was Solomon's father, not his son.

items.text: Jesus remained three years in the tomb.
items.note: He remained there three days.

items.text: The prophet Jonah was sent to preach in Jerusalem.
items.note: He was sent to Nineveh.

items.text: It was Moses who led the people across the Jordan on dry ground.
items.note: It was Joshua; Moses crossed the Red Sea.

items.text: Noah's ark came to rest on Mount Sinai.
items.note: It came to rest on Mount Ararat.

items.text: The prophet Elijah was swallowed by a great fish.
items.note: It was Jonah who was swallowed.

items.text: The Ten Commandments were engraved on three tablets of stone.
items.note: They were on two tablets.

items.text: Judas Iscariot was replaced by the apostle Paul.
items.note: He was replaced by Matthias.

items.text: During the temptation, Jesus turned stones into bread.
items.note: He refused to do it.

items.text: David was the son of King Saul.
items.note: David was the son of Jesse.

items.text: Job's wife advised him to remain faithful to God.
items.note: She said to him, "Curse God, and die!"

items.text: King Solomon made the Ark of the Covenant.
items.note: It was made in the wilderness during the time of Moses.

items.text: The prophet Daniel lived during the time of Moses.
items.note: He lived during the exile in Babylon.

items.text: The wise men offered Jesus gold, silver, and bronze.
items.note: They offered him gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

items.text: Jesus was betrayed by the apostle Thomas.
items.note: He was betrayed by Judas.

items.text: The giant Goliath was a friend and ally of David.
items.note: He was David's enemy.

items.text: King Herod was the father of Pontius Pilate.
items.note: They had no family relation.

items.text: Adam and Eve had only two sons, Cain and Abel.
items.note: They also had Seth and other children.

items.text: The prophet Isaiah was thrown into the lion's den.
items.note: It was Daniel who was thrown in.

items.text: The wise men found the child Jesus in a stable.
items.note: They entered "the house": the visit happened later than we imagine.

items.text: According to the Gospels, Jesus fell three times while carrying his cross.
items.note: The three falls come from tradition, not from the biblical text.

items.text: Delilah shaved Samson's hair herself.
items.note: She called a man to shave the seven locks.

items.text: "Help yourself, and heaven will help you" is a verse from the Bible.
items.note: This is a quote from La Fontaine, not from the Bible.

items.text: Jesus sat down to teach the Sermon on the Mount.
items.note: "He sat down, and his disciples came to him."

items.text: The shortest verse in the Bible is "Jesus wept."
items.note: Two words at the tomb of Lazarus.

items.text: The New Testament tells us that Peter was crucified upside down.
items.note: This is an ancient tradition absent from the biblical text.

items.text: Jonah fled in the direction of Nineveh.
items.note: He fled the OPPOSITE way, toward Tarshish — Nineveh was his mission.

items.text: Four men lowered the paralyzed man through the roof in front of Jesus.
items.note: They uncovered the roof, because there was no room at the door.

items.text: Moses spoke to the rock, just as God had commanded him.
items.note: He struck it twice — this cost him entry into the Promised Land.

items.text: Jesus remained on earth for forty days after his resurrection.
items.note: He appeared to his followers for forty days before the ascension.

items.text: The letter to the Hebrews clearly names its author.
items.note: The author is never named — the only NT book in this case among the epistles.

items.text: Jael killed the general Sisera with a tent peg.
items.note: She drove it through him while he slept.

items.text: Adam and Eve were driven from the garden for eating from the tree of life.
items.note: It was the tree of the KNOWLEDGE of good and evil; the tree of life was later forbidden to them.

items.text: Goliath was about three meters tall.
items.note: Six cubits and a span, about 9.5 feet.

items.text: Mary and Joseph offered two doves in the temple for Jesus.
items.note: The offering of poor families.

items.text: Jesus wrote a book of the New Testament.
items.note: Jesus left no writings; the Gospels testify to him.

items.text: In the account of Eden, the serpent is called "Satan."
items.note: Genesis says "the serpent"; the identification comes from Revelation.

items.text: Paul and Silas sang hymns at midnight in the prison at Philippi.
items.note: And the other prisoners were listening to them.

items.text: An angel opened the prison doors at Philippi to free Paul and Silas.
items.note: It was an earthquake — the angel was for Peter in Jerusalem.

items.text: Abraham sacrificed a lamb in place of Isaac.
items.note: It was a RAM, caught by the horns in a bush.

items.text: According to Matthew, the star stopped directly over the place where the child was.
items.note: It went before the wise men and came to rest.

items.text: David wrote all the Psalms.
items.note: Asaph, the sons of Korah, Solomon, and Moses also wrote some.

items.text: Daniel refused to eat the food of the king of Babylon.
items.note: He resolved not to defile himself, and requested vegetables.

items.text: The prophet Enoch died very old, like the other patriarchs.
items.note: He "was not, because God took him" — taken up without experiencing death.

items.text: God created light before creating the sun.
items.note: Light appears on the first day, the sun and moon on the fourth.

items.text: Adam was created on the first day of creation.
items.note: Mankind is created on the sixth day, last of all.

items.text: Noah first released a dove to see if the waters had subsided.
items.note: He first released a raven, then the dove.

items.text: Noah brought seven pairs of all clean animals into the ark.
items.note: Seven pairs for clean animals, one pair for unclean.

items.text: After the flood, Noah planted a vineyard and became drunk.
items.note: The first episode after leaving the ark: the vineyard, the wine, the shame.

items.text: Abraham negotiated with God down to five righteous people to spare Sodom.
items.note: He bargained from fifty down to ten righteous, not five.

items.text: Abraham received tithes from Melchizedek.
items.note: It's the opposite: Abraham gave a tenth of everything to Melchizedek.

items.text: Jacob wrestled all night and was struck on the hip socket.
items.note: He limped from it, and received the name Israel.

items.text: Joseph was thirty years old when his brothers sold him.
items.note: He was seventeen; at thirty he appeared before Pharaoh.

items.text: Joseph's brothers sold him for thirty pieces of silver.
items.note: Twenty shekels of silver. The thirty pieces belong to Judas.

items.text: Moses was about eighty years old when he spoke to Pharaoh.
items.note: Moses was 80 years old, Aaron was 83.

items.text: The Red Sea opened the moment Moses stretched out his hand.
items.note: The Lord drove back the sea by a strong east wind all night.

items.text: The manna tasted like a cake sweetened with honey.
items.note: White as coriander seed, and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey.

items.text: Moses went up Mount Sinai twice to receive the tablets of stone.
items.note: The first tablets were broken after the golden calf.

items.text: Aaron entered the Promised Land with the people.
items.note: He died on Mount Hor, before entering Canaan.

items.text: Aaron's staff budded and produced almonds.
items.note: A sign that God had chosen the tribe of Levi.

items.text: Balaam's donkey spoke.
items.note: The Lord opened the donkey's mouth.

items.text: Joshua prayed and the sun stood still during a battle.
items.note: The sun stood still over Gibeon, and the moon over Aijalon.

items.text: Samson killed three hundred men with the jawbone of a donkey.
items.note: A thousand men. The three hundred were his foxes.

items.text: Samson was married to Delilah.
items.note: The Bible never says they were married; his wife was from Timnah.

items.text: Ruth was the grandmother of King David.
items.note: His great-grandmother: Ruth, Obed, Jesse, David.

items.text: The young Samuel ran to Eli three times, thinking it was he who called.
items.note: On the third time, Eli understood it was the Lord.

items.text: David spared King Saul's life twice.
items.note: In the cave of En Gedi, then in Saul's sleeping camp.

items.text: King Saul died by the hand of a Philistine soldier.
items.note: Wounded by the archers, he fell on his own sword.

items.text: David lived for a time among the Philistines, at Ziklag.
items.note: Fleeing Saul, he settled for sixteen months in Philistine territory.

items.text: Goliath had a brother, who was also killed by one of David's mighty men.
items.note: Elhanan killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath.

items.text: Michal admired David when he danced before the ark.
items.note: She despised him in her heart when she saw him leaping and dancing.

items.text: Solomon uttered one thousand five hundred proverbs.
items.note: Three thousand proverbs, and one thousand five songs.

items.text: Solomon's temple was built without the sound of hammer on the site.
items.note: The stones were dressed at the quarry before being brought there.

items.text: Solomon reigned sixty years over Israel.
items.note: Forty years, like his father David.

items.text: After Solomon, the kingdom was divided into two: Israel and Judah.
items.note: Ten tribes in the north under Jeroboam, Judah in the south under Rehoboam.

items.text: Elisha raised the dead son of the widow of Zarephath.
items.note: It was Elijah. Elisha raised the son of the Shunnamite woman.

items.text: Strengthened by a single meal, Elijah walked forty days to Horeb.
items.note: A cake and water brought by an angel.

items.text: Elisha asked for a double portion of Elijah's spirit.
items.note: "Please let a double portion of your spirit be upon me."

items.text: A dead man came to life when he touched the bones of Elisha.
items.note: Thrown into Elisha's tomb, the man rose to his feet.

items.text: Jezebel died thrown from a window, and the dogs devoured her.
items.note: As Elijah had declared.

items.text: The bronze serpent of Moses was destroyed centuries later by King Hezekiah.
items.note: The people were burning incense to it; Hezekiah broke it into pieces.

items.text: For King Hezekiah, the shadow moved forward ten degrees on Ahaz' sundial.
items.note: It moved back ten degrees — a sign of his healing.

items.text: The kingdom of Judah fell before the kingdom of Israel.
items.note: Israel (Samaria) fell first, facing Assyria.

items.text: King Uzziah was struck with leprosy for offering incense in the temple.
items.note: He encroached on the priests' role and remained leprous until his death.

items.text: The exile in Babylon was to last seventy years according to Jeremiah.
items.note: A prophecy recalled by Daniel and fulfilled under Cyrus.

items.text: It was King Nebuchadnezzar who authorized the return of the exiles to Jerusalem.
items.note: It was Cyrus, king of Persia, by a decree.

items.text: Nehemiah rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem in one hundred twenty days.
items.note: In fifty-two days, despite opposition.

items.text: Esther was the niece of Mordecai.
items.note: His cousin: she was the daughter of his uncle.

items.text: The name of God does not appear even once in the book of Esther.
items.note: And yet his providence shines on every page.

items.text: Job recovered exactly what he had lost, no more and no less.
items.note: The Lord restored to him twice as much as he had before.

items.text: God commended the three friends of Job for their wise words.
items.note: His wrath burned against them: they had not spoken what is right.

items.text: Psalm 23 is the shortest chapter in the Bible.
items.note: The shortest is Psalm 117: two verses.

items.text: The book of Proverbs was written entirely by Solomon.
items.note: Agur and King Lemuel also wrote some.

items.text: Isaiah walked naked and barefoot for three years.
items.note: A prophetic sign against Egypt and Ethiopia.

items.text: Ezekiel had to lie on his left side for forty days.
items.note: Three hundred ninety days on the left; the forty was on the right.

items.text: Jonah rejoiced when he saw Nineveh repent.
items.note: This displeased him greatly, and he became angry.

items.text: Daniel was thrown to the lions for refusing to eat the king's food.
items.note: It was because he prayed three times a day despite the decree.

items.text: In the furnace, they saw four men when three had been thrown in.
items.note: "The appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods."

items.text: The prophet Zechariah saw in a vision a flying scroll.
items.note: A flying scroll of twenty cubits by ten.

items.text: Two books of the Bible bear the name of a woman.
items.note: Ruth and Esther.

items.text: According to the Gospels, John the Baptist performed no miracles.
items.note: "John did no sign, but all things that John spoke about this man were true."

items.text: Jesus wept on two occasions according to the Gospels.
items.note: At the tomb of Lazarus, and over Jerusalem.

items.text: When Jesus cursed the fig tree, it was the season for figs.
items.note: "It was not the season for figs" — the tree had leaves only.

items.text: Jesus healed Peter's mother-in-law, who was suffering from fever.
items.note: So Peter was married. She got up and served them.

items.text: Of ten lepers healed, only one came back to thank Jesus — a Samaritan.
items.note: "Where are the nine?"

items.text: In the parable, the older brother welcomed the prodigal son with joy.
items.note: He became angry and refused to enter.

items.text: Jesus drove out the money changers from the temple with a whip made of cords.
items.note: He overturned the tables of the money changers.

items.text: The inscription on the cross was written in Hebrew, Greek, and Egyptian.
items.note: In Hebrew, Latin, and Greek.

items.text: The soldiers broke Jesus' legs on the cross.
items.note: Finding him already dead, they did not break his legs — Scripture was fulfilled.

items.text: It was Joseph of Arimathea who brought myrrh and aloes to bury Jesus.
items.note: It was Nicodemus — about one hundred pounds of spices.

items.text: Peter was the first to enter the empty tomb.
items.note: John arrived first, running, but did not enter.

items.text: The risen Jesus refused to eat in front of his disciples.
items.note: He ate broiled fish in front of them, to prove he was not a spirit.

items.text: Jesus appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once.
items.note: Paul notes that most were still alive.

items.text: Matthias was chosen by a show of hands vote to replace Judas.
items.note: The lot fell on Matthias, after prayer.
